name: SequenceTree Turn Mode
description: Decides per prompt which research-suite hooks and gates run: skip, light, research, code or deep

globalState.previousMode: the mode the previous turn ran in, or none

classify.label: What kind of turn is this?

config.instructions: Classify the user's prompt (state.prompt) in a coding session on SequenceTree, a C++ JUCE plugin. Pick the one option that describes what the user is asking for in this message. A prompt that asks for code to be written or changed is code or deep even if it also asks a question. A prompt that only asks about code, research, a plan or how code should be designed is research. Short replies and conversational steering are control.

options.label: A control command that steers the conversation without asking for new work: stop, wait, hurry up, move on, continue, go ahead, yes, no, or a short reply to a question
A simple question or basic command that can be answered directly, without reading through or changing code

A research, analysis, explanation, review, design or planning question: understanding how code works, comparing approaches, how code should be structured, looking something up, or writing a plan, with no code being written or changed
A routine request to write, generate, change, fix, rename, refactor or delete code, including any change to the audio thread or the traversal
An in-depth coding request: a new feature, or a change across several files or classes

reply.label: Does the reply carry on the previous turn's work?

config.instructions: state.prompt is a short reply or steering command. state.previousMode is the mode the previous turn ran in (skip, light, research, code, deep, or none for the first turn). Decide whether the reply approves or continues code work - yes, go ahead, do it, continue, keep going - or only steers or answers without asking for code work.

options.label: Steers or answers without asking for code work, or state.previousMode is skip, light or none
Approves or continues code work, and state.previousMode is research or code
Approves or continues code work, and state.previousMode is deep

config.description: Code change with the design-rule and readability gates, with no route of its own.
config.directive: Write the change under the Key Design Rules; the design-rule and readability gates check it when the turn ends.

config.description: No gates and no extra checks for this turn.
config.directive: Do what the command says. Run no design-rule, readability or systematic checks.
Answer directly. No rule recitation, no audit and no gates; the Key Design Rules still bind any code written.
config.context: Light mode: answer directly. No rule recitation, no audit and no gates this turn. The Key Design Rules still bind any code you write, and an edit under Source still runs the design-rule and readability gates. The user requests the full verification protocol by putting -deep in their prompt.

config.directive: Answer from the real code: name the actual functions, files and call sites. Do not run the design-rule or readability gates; no code is being changed.
config.context: Research mode: analysis counts as work, so the systematic principles apply to this answer. Name the real functions, files and call sites, and answer readability for the code you read. No design-rule or readability gate runs this turn unless you edit Source. The user requests the full verification protocol by putting -deep in their prompt.

config.description: Full protocol: gates plus the change trees at Stop.
config.directive: Run the full verification protocol: the prompt step has already run the design-rule audit on the diff, and the design-rule, readability and change trees check it again when the turn ends.
